articles.headline: Zomba Teacher Uses Traditional Dance to Bring Girls Back to School
articles.preview: Mulinga Primary School teacher Bertha Mlundira used Manganje and Mganda performances to encourage girls who have not returned after the holiday to go back to class.
articles.content: A primary school teacher in Zomba District has turned to traditional dance and community mobilisation to encourage girls who have not returned to school after the holiday to go back to the classroom. The initiative, led by Bertha Mlundira, a teacher at Mulinga Primary School in Chikomwe Zone, was conducted on Wednesday in villages surrounding the school through the Sisters in Success Club, an extracurricular initiative she founded to encourage girls to remain in school, build confidence and pursue their future aspirations. Mlundira said the campaign followed concerns that some girls had failed to return to school after the long holiday, with some reportedly getting married while others had simply chosen to remain at home. Rather than limiting the campaign to conventional home visits, Mlundira and members of the initiative used Manganje and Mganda traditional performances to reach out to the girls and their families, creating a community-centred approach to encouraging them to return to school. “We planned a community walk to visit their homes and encourage them to return to school. During the walk, we performed different cultural activities, including Manganje and Mganda. The campaign has worked, as several girls have promised that we will see them at school on Monday,” Mlundira said. She said parents had also welcomed the initiative, describing the response from the community as encouraging. The Sisters in Success Club was established by Mlundira as an extracurricular platform aimed at empowering girls to stay in school, develop confidence, and acquire the determination needed to shape their own future. The campaign comes as a reminder of the role teachers, parents, and communities can play in identifying girls at risk of dropping out and encouraging them to return to education.

articles.headline: Bangwe CDSS Teacher Philip Kalindo Dies
articles.preview: The education community in Blantyre is mourning the death of Philip Kalindo, a teacher at Bangwe Community Day Secondary School.
articles.content: The education community in Blantyre is mourning the death of Philip Kalindo, a teacher at Bangwe Community Day Secondary School (CDSS). Kalindo, who was also the twin brother of Bon Kalindo, reportedly reported for duty at the school today before his death was confirmed. Circumstances surrounding his death have not yet been disclosed. Details of the funeral and burial arrangements will be communicated later as the family makes the necessary arrangements.

articles.headline: Community Members Storm Samama Primary School Over Abduction Claim
articles.preview: Community members reportedly stormed a school in Mangochi armed with machetes and hammers after a learner claimed a teacher was involved in his abduction.
articles.content: Drama unfolded at Samama Primary School in Koche Zone, Mangochi District, on Wednesday morning after some community members reportedly stormed the school armed with machetes and hammers, following a learner’s alleged claim that a teacher had been involved in his abduction. The incident reportedly began after a Standard 6 learner allegedly told community members that a teacher at the school had helped hand the learner over to people who allegedly abducted him. The learner was reportedly later found in a forest in Mangochi town. Angered by the claim, some community members reportedly rushed to the school, where they allegedly threatened and assaulted some teachers. The headteacher alerted police, who quickly responded to the situation together with Mangochi District education officials. Information gathered during the ensuing inquiry indicates that the learner later told police that the allegations against the teacher were false and that the claim had been made deliberately to get the teacher into trouble. Further checks also established that the learner did not report for classes on the day of the incident. Authorities are continuing with investigations to establish the full circumstances surrounding the allegations and the subsequent confrontation at the school. Education Matters will continue following the story and provide updates as further information is verified.

articles.headline: Nangongo Primary School Teacher Arrested Over Allegations
articles.preview: A primary school teacher in Machinga has been arrested following allegations of a sexual relationship with a Standard 8 learner.
articles.content: A primary school teacher in Machinga has been arrested following allegations that he had a sexual relationship with a Standard 8 learner. The teacher, identified as Patrick Chitsulo, is reportedly based at Nangongo Primary School in Kayuni Zone. According to the allegations, Chitsulo had a sexual relationship with the learner, who is said to have become pregnant. He is currently in police custody at Nselema Police Station as investigations into the matter continue. The allegations have not yet been tested in court, and the suspect is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

articles.headline: Promote Teachers Who Excel
articles.preview: Hardworking teachers deserve meaningful career progression, not just certificates.
articles.content: A hardworking teacher should not have to remain on the same grade year after year while their exceptional performance is rewarded with nothing more than a certificate. If a teacher consistently delivers outstanding results, transforms learners' performance and goes beyond the call of duty, that achievement should be recognised through meaningful career progression. Promote teachers who excel. Reward performance with opportunity. When hard work has a clear path to promotion, teachers have a greater incentive to give their best, and the education system stands to benefit.

articles.headline: Duwana wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy
articles.preview: FDuwana wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy
articles.content: Duwama Muhammad, msungwana waku Mangochi uja yemwe adalemba yekha mayeso a sitandade 8 pa sukulu ya pulayimale ya Mangale, tsopano wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy. Malingana ndi uthenga omwe a Maranatha Academy atulutsa, msungwanayu achita maphunziro ake kusukuluyi mwa ulele potsatira thandizo la maphunziro lomwe eni sukuluyi adapereka (full scholarship).  Mkulu wa Maranatha Academy Dr. Ernest Kaonga wati sukuluyi ndiyokhudzidwa ndi nkhani ya Duwama komanso mtima wake osagonja. "Anzake ena omwe anakumana ndi zomwe iyeyu anadutsamozi, adangonja kalekale. Tili ndi chikhulupiliro mwa msungwanayu, kuti adzakhala mtsogoleri ndipo kamba ka ichi aphunzira kusukulu zathu mwa ulere mpaka form 4," anatero a Kaonga.  Mbali yake, Duwama wayamikira mwini wake wa Maranatha Academy, Dr. Kaonga kamba komukhulupilira.  by Innocent Kumchedwa.

articles.headline: Honorable Shadric Namalomba officially opened a girls' hostel
articles.preview: Mangochi South East Member of Parliament and Minister of Information Shadric Namalomba has today officially opened a girls' hostel
articles.content: Mangochi South East Member of Parliament and Minister of Information Shadric Namalomba has today officially opened a girls' hostel at Chilipa Community Day Secondary School in Mangochi. Constructed with funding from the Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) programme, the hostel has capacity to accommodate more than 50 girls. The facility is expected to improve girls' access to secondary education by providing accommodation closer to the school, particularly for learners who previously travelled long distances to attend classes.
